There's a deep duality between the two environments. Both are about a less-sophisticated principal trying to get ideal outcomes from a set of more-sophisticated agents: in the first case, the principal is a static algorithm and the agents are humans, in the second case, the principal is humans plus weaker LLMs and the agents are stronger LLMs.

A key finding was that you can achieve much better outcomes if you can guarantee limits to how much agents can collude (see: Nash equilibria being abundant, vs. cooperative-game-theory "cores" often being empty). That argument should naturally transfer to this new setting.

I guess it's important to distinguish between "trading" and "investing" as well. 

Imo, buying something with no SL and just HODL-ing isn't trading- that's investing. Most of these memecoin "traders" aren't trading, they are gambling and/or "investing" with a zero or hero mindset. There is no defined risk, no invalidation, and oftentimes no real target. That to me is closer to "investing" than "trading" but again really just gambling more than anything.

Trading is buying something with an entry, invalidation (SL either hard or soft) and target. Risk is measured/defined, and HODL-ing is not really a thing (when you cross that line from trading with a set inval to buying and HODL-ing that is a cross from trading to investing). In actual trading, opportunity cost isn't a very relevant concept because leverage (when used correctly) removes capital constraints for the most part. 

In investing, opportunity cost is absolutely relevant, but for someone who knows how to actively trade (with leverage), it becomes much less relevant- as they are always able to chase other opportunities in their "trading" ports while their investing port may remain "dormant". 

Where opportunity cost is absolutely the most relevant imo is when you have someone who doesn't know how to actually trade and only invests- for these people, opportunity cost should be a pretty significant consideration when making their investment decisions imo.
